title: The whole server on one page
one_liner: A client talks to a forked backend. SQL goes through parse, rewrite, plan and execute. Rows live in 8kB pages behind shared buffers. WAL keeps it safe and feeds replicas.
analogy: A restaurant: the host seats you (postmaster), your waiter takes the order (backend), the kitchen follows a recipe (planner and executor), the pantry is shared (buffers and files), and a logbook records everything (WAL).
big_picture: One postmaster forks one backend process per client.
SQL text passes four stages: parser, rewriter, planner, executor.
The executor reads and writes 8kB pages through shared buffers.
Every change is logged in WAL before the page is written.
Helper processes flush pages, vacuum old rows and stream WAL to replicas.

flow.detail: Client connects, postmaster forks a backend, backend authenticates.
SQL text becomes a tree, names are resolved against catalogs.
Views are replaced by the queries behind them.
Plan nodes pull rows one at a time.
Table and index code goes through shared buffers to data files.
WAL record flushed first, then commit is durable.
